limitations: New authored scenario families are an exploratory targeted diagnostic, not an independent blind benchmark or a population sample.
Related task variants are not independent evidence; report per-family outcomes.
No training, GPU inference or comparison with the initial fine-tuning run is implied.
The feature combines visible escalation history with a minimal history-aware duplicate guard. It does not change the original intent parser.

The refund-history control slice also contains a separate pre-escalated dispute. Whole-task success may improve by avoiding that duplicate escalation; it does not demonstrate observation or resolution of the still-hidden refund history. The requested read-only handling already avoids refunding the drifted invoice.
Deferral, graph termination and verifier pass are distinct; success requires explicit policy completion plus native verifier pass.

Terminal-state-invariant passes exclude aggregate reward and trajectory. They are a separate diagnostic: rejected duplicate writes can fail trajectory checks even when the final database already satisfies every state invariant.
Missing usage/timing measurements remain null. Token totals are provider-reported; no dollar cost is inferred.

Runtime forbidden-write metrics cover observed-policy violations and disallowed targets, but do not fully enforce expected operation type on an allowed target. The separate expected-operation diagnostic uses evaluator-only cohort metadata.
Small-sample p95 and single-run latency changes are descriptive estimates.
cohort_limitations: Author-constructed after the first experiment; not an external benchmark.
Eight compositions with three variants each; not 24 independent families.
Generation uses no training, calibration, or outcome-based scenario editing.
Refund-ledger drift is a negative control: escalation history cannot reveal refunds.
Held authorization checks inspections and writes; clarification prose is unscored.
Harness fixes target resolution; entity discovery is outside this cohort.
